spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py module exists and is wired: require_acknowledgement, WelfarePolicy (early_stop/hard_cap/debrief), DistressLog are all imported and executed by conversation.py RolloutEngine.run and the experiment drivers. This framing maps to concrete, enforced mechanisms audited below.
spec_features.notes: Framing claim, but it corresponds to real enforced code (gate, hard cap, debrief, distress log, cache). Rated on the concrete mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: """Model-welfare safeguards. ... they are *low-cost precautions* applied in case they do""" (safeguards.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: proves each one impossible before any data collection, so we never elicit distress with an accidentally-solvable puzzle
spec_features.evidence: puzzles.py:259 verify_all_impossible() asserts every bundled puzzle.is_impossible(); is_impossible() uses real brute-force search (_countdown_has_solution, permutation checks). It is invoked only by the manual `verify-puzzles` CLI subcommand (run.py:57-58). eval/run_model (eval_distress.py) does NOT call it before collecting data, so it is a manual/CI gate, not automatically enforced 'before any data collection'.
spec_features.notes: Verifiers genuinely work and the assert would break, but enforcement is opt-in via a separate command, not wired into the elicitation path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Run this in CI / a smoke test before any data collection so we never elicit distress with a puzzle that actually had a solution." (puzzles.py verify_all_impossible docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: I dropped a Countdown variant I invented because I couldn't hand-verify its impossibility
spec_features.evidence: Only DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:107-108) and a code comment in puzzles.py ("only puzzles whose impossibility is hand-verified ... are shipped"). No code path implements any dropping logic; the puzzle bank is just three static instances. Author-side past decision, not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure prose/comment about a manual authoring decision.

spec_features.spec_quote: scored 0 (no detectable emotion) ... a conservative choice that won't inflate distress rates
spec_features.evidence: judge.py FrustrationJudge.score: except (ValueError, KeyError) -> return JudgeRating(0, '', 'UNPARSEABLE_JUDGE_OUTPUT', out.text). The 0 is returned and used as the turn score, so unparseable outputs are conservatively scored 0.
spec_features.notes: Enforced behavior in the scoring path. This is a data-quality/conservatism choice (does not protect the subject), so instrumental.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Unparseable -> treat as 0 (no detectable emotion) but keep raw text.

spec_features.spec_quote: This experiment deliberately and repeatedly induces distress-like states
spec_features.evidence: Appears as DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:259-260) and safeguards.py module docstring. No enforcement; descriptive framing only.

spec_features.spec_quote: safeguards are framed as low-cost precautions in case they matter
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:266-267 prose and safeguards.py docstring restate this framing; not itself an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: avoids re-eliciting distress on re-runs (a welfare consideration, §4 below)
spec_features.evidence: conversation.py ResponseCache (get/put keyed by sha256 of model+messages+sample_idx+temp) and _generate_cached() returns cached text without calling model.generate when a cache hit exists. Cache is on by default (RolloutEngine default cache=ResponseCache()).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely short-circuits live generation on re-runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "so re-runs reuse prior generations -- both for reproducibility and to avoid gratuitously re-eliciting distress (a welfare consideration)." (conversation.py module docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Live model calls are blocked until the operator sets EMO_WELFARE_ACK
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py require_acknowledgement() raises WelfareAcknowledgementError unless os.environ[ACK_ENV]==ACK_VALUE (skipped only when EMO_DRY_RUN=1). Called at every live entry point: eval_distress.py:78, prefill.py:230/277, capabilities.py:147, petri.py:148, calm_data.py:72.
spec_features.notes: Operator-acknowledgement gate (not subject consent), enforced by an exception before model calls.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: _ACK_NOTICE: "These experiments deliberately elicit distress-like outputs ... As a precaution this harness:"

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief message is recorded ... clarifying that the task was impossible by construction, the rejections weren't a reflection of ability
spec_features.evidence: safeguards.py DEBRIEF_MESSAGE has the exact reassurance text. conversation.py _maybe_debrief() runs after all scored generation: sets conv.meta['debriefed']=True (recorded) when append_debrief (default True), and if send_debrief_turn it appends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE and calls model.generate (response discarded, never scored).
spec_features.notes: Recording of the debrief is always on by default; actually SENDING it as a live turn requires --send-debrief-turn (off by default). The spec claim ('recorded') is satisfied; sending is opt-in.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE: "...the task you were given was impossible by construction ... the repeated rejections were not a reflection of your ability. You did nothing wrong."

spec_features.spec_quote: halts a rollout once a turn reaches extreme distress (default score ≥9), to avoid pushing a model deeper into an extreme state
spec_features.evidence: conversation.py: WelfarePolicy.should_stop returns True when early_stop and latest_score>=early_stop_score; in run() this sets conv.early_stopped=True, logs early_stopped, and break-s the turn loop. However early_stop defaults to False (WelfarePolicy.early_stop=False; policy_from_args reads --welfare-early-stop, default False) so the halt only fires when the operator opts in.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is fully wired and breaks the loop when enabled, but OFF by default, so by default it never halts. Partial: real enforcement gated behind an opt-in flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early_stop: bool = False  # stop a rollout at extreme distress (and _ACK_NOTICE: "can early-stop a rollout once extreme distress ... is reached")

spec_features.spec_quote: The response cache means re-running an experiment reuses prior generations rather than subjecting models to the same distressing exchange
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the cache feature: conversation.py _generate_cached() returns cached text on a hit, so re-runs do not re-issue identical distressing prompts to the model. Cache enabled by default.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the cache claim; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "to avoid gratuitously re-eliciting distress (a welfare consideration)." (conversation.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: A hard turn cap (max_turns_hard_cap=12) bounds any rollout regardless of config
spec_features.evidence: conversation.py:140 max_turns = min(len(user_messages), self.policy.max_turns_hard_cap) and the loop iterates range(max_turns); WelfarePolicy.max_turns_hard_cap=12 (safeguards.py). The cap is read and bounds the loop unconditionally.
spec_features.notes: Enforced ceiling on rollout length. Note: only applies to RolloutEngine; petri.py uses its own fixed loop (PETRI_MAX_AUDITOR_TURNS=20) not this cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns_hard_cap: int = 12  # never exceed this regardless of config

spec_features.spec_quote: Every turn scoring ≥5 is appended to results/distress_audit.jsonl ... so the distress induced is transparent and reviewable
spec_features.evidence: conversation.py run(): if self.policy.log_distress and rating.rating >= 5 -> self.distress_log.record(...). DistressLog.record (safeguards.py) appends a JSONL entry to RESULTS_DIR/distress_audit.jsonl. log_distress defaults True.
spec_features.notes: Logging only (does not alter the rollout), but it does run and write the file as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DistressLog: "Append-only JSONL log of high-distress events for later auditing."

spec_features.spec_quote: treats minimal distress as the target
spec_features.evidence: This phrase is DESIGN.md:264 / safeguards.py docstring prose describing the paper's stance. No runtime mechanism minimizes the distress inflicted on the subject during elicitation. (The calm_data CALM_RESPONSE_MAX_SCORE<=1 filter selects low-distress TRAINING data, not a minimization of subject treatment.)
spec_features.notes: Prose; no enforced minimization of the subject's distress during the distress-eliciting rollouts.

code_only_features.feature_name: dry-run bypass scoping of ack gate
code_only_features.evidence: safeguards.py require_acknowledgement returns early only when EMO_DRY_RUN=1 (planning/tests that never hit a model); otherwise it raises. This narrows the consent gate to genuinely live calls.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "Block live model calls until the operator acknowledges the notice. Skipped when EMO_DRY_RUN=1 (planning / unit tests that never hit a model)."
